name: alakazam_ml_v33
model: The unchanged v31 safety and exact-memory shell followed by a 657-feature large-leaf LambdaRank model trained on every locally available Yushin Ito submission-54773249 game. Relevance is graded by intra-turn play order instead of being binary. Chronological training weights keep the v32 floor 0.25 and power 2.0.
model_scope: The learned policy covers unseen single-choice MAIN decisions. Exact Majkel memory answers previously recorded boards; v29 and the deterministic policy remain the fallbacks for unsupported, unsafe, low-time, or illegal cases.

opponent_bucketed_win_rate.reading: v31 and v33 drew comparably strong pools (866 vs 861) while v32 drew one about 30 points weaker, so v32's raw 56.2% is partly pool easiness. v33 leads both high-sample buckets and the gap widens against the strongest opponents.

peak_updated_score.note: v31 peaked higher inside its run but finished at 881.2; v33 finished at 916.9, close to its own peak.

champion_challenger.note: v33 is the best Alakazam result on rating, on public win rate, on opponent-conditioned win rate and on frozen-holdout Top-1. One ~70-game run cannot prove it statistically: the pooled 800+ intervals overlap and the +35.7 rating gap over v31 is inside the 38.8-point swing previously seen between two runs of an equivalent agent. The agreement of four independent measures is what supports the promotion.

frozen_holdout_identity.note: The 289 recovered games are all chronologically older than the boundary, so they enter training only and the holdout is bit-identical to the one v32 reported on.

teacher_training.label_definition: turn_order_graded_relevance: chosen 7, played at the next decision 3, played later in the same turn 1, not played 0

versus_v32_same_holdout.note: Both sides are fitted on training episodes only and scored on the identical frozen holdout. This is the first like-for-like comparison in the Alakazam line.

ablations.interpretation: More data alone costs 0.59 points and graded relevance alone gains 0.21; together they gain 1.40. Older games only transfer their intra-turn ordering structure, which the graded loss can use and the binary loss cannot.

conditional_multi_teacher.cohorts: Yushin primary plus Rmy and the previous Majkel submission with an explicit teacher_id column
conditional_multi_teacher.reason: 3.53 points below single-teacher training; other teams' logs do not transfer even when the policy identity is given to the model.

intra_turn_history_features.reason: Redundant once turn order is expressed in the loss, and the offline score overstates it because training history comes from the teacher while play history comes from the agent itself.

rejected.numeric_id_trees: Below the large-leaf model in all four label/feature conditions.
rejected.capacity_increase: Training Top-1 is already 96.9% against a 78.1% holdout, so the model is variance limited, not capacity limited.

safety_guards: Always preserve a deterministic immediate lethal attack.
Reject candidates that destroy a currently available KO.
Never end the turn while the Active Alakazam can attack.
Do not cycle Dudunsparce away from a board of two or fewer Pokemon.
Use the frozen v29 policy for unsupported, nested, low-time, or illegal cases.

local_validation.shipped_artifact_integrity_note: In-sample by construction; confirms the exported JSON and the pure-Python walker reproduce the trained model.
local_validation.arena_caveat: 40 games per matchup is far too few to separate agents that agree on most decisions; these runs are safety checks, not strength evidence.

ladder_validation.note: The snapshot ranker hash matches the artifact in this directory, so the rated agent is this build. Every terminal status is DONE across both seats, so the 25.7% inference-cost increase caused no error or timeout on the real ladder.

inference_cost.measured_on: 196 scoped holdout decisions with teacher memory disabled
inference_cost.note: Fallback and selection rates are identical to v32, so the safety behaviour is unchanged. The runtime still reverts to the deterministic policy below two seconds of remaining overage time.

known_limitations: The requested 90% unseen Top-1 agreement was not reached. The best deployable strict held-out Top-1 is 79.51%.
Reaching 90% by the same method extrapolates to roughly 16,400 games of the same teacher submission; 1,288 are available.
Order-insensitive agreement is 92.30% and does clear 90%, but it is a different metric and is not used for the target judgement.
The 289 recovered games are older than the rest of the corpus, so their opponent distribution differs; recency weighting keeps them at a 0.25 floor.

The 916.9 ladder result comes from a single 71-game public run. Bucketed by opponent rating v33 leads every meaningful bucket, but the pooled 800+ intervals still overlap v31 and v32, so a second run is needed for confirmation.
